messages:
Maya (support): Priya from Acme reports p99 jump to ~12s and user-facing timeouts. Started ~09:12 UTC after a deploy. She says requests are getting 'admit timeout' and many are queued.
Priya (Acme): Yep, started right after you pushed the batching changes. Repro for us: ~1k concurrent small prompts => p99 spikes, p95 also worse. Trace id: trace-acme-2026-03-17-09:13:45.
Maya (support): Adding eng-runtime and oncall. Priya shared a small curl repro, pasted below.
Priya (Acme): curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":8}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -v  # repeat x1000
deploy-bot: Deployed commit f2e3b7d (eng-runtime) at 2026-03-17T09:08:22Z — config: default-batching-v2 enabled in prod.
Omar (eng-runtime): Looking. Initial hunch: the new batching-v2 introduced a windowing change and different worker affinity. Might increase per-worker queueing under tail traffic.
Aaron (oncall-sre): I see admission backpressure > 80% on us-east-1 pool since 09:10. Concurrency limit reached on several shards, and the admit queue depth grew.
Internal QA Bot: Alert: p99 latency > 8s (us-east-1), affected routes: /v1/generate (tenants: acme-corp, sandbox).
Liu (eng-platform): Can you paste the worker metrics? CPU/GPU saturation?
Aaron (oncall-sre): GPU util on affected workers ~70-75%, but busy-for-long spike in event loop. Worker process backlog (req_wait) climbing.
Maya (support): Priya — can you confirm whether they were using chunked streaming or single-shot?
Priya (Acme): Single-shot requests from our end. Small prompts, lots of them.
Omar (eng-runtime): That matches: batching-v2 groups small prompts into larger batches which can raise scheduling latency when the batch window waits for more items. Under high concurrency it can cause hot shards to accumulate.
Omar (eng-runtime): Repro idea: run 600 parallel single-shot requests with 8-token responses to the same model variant and watch admit queue.
Maya (support): Priya can reproduce locally with the curl loop. She confirmed consistent p99 > 10s.
Aaron (oncall-sre): Short-term mitigation: disable batching-v2 or fall back to batching-v1 for affected pool. Also increase admission concurrency soft-limit by 20% for that pool to let more inflight while we investigate.
Liu (eng-platform): I can flip a runtime flag to disable batching-v2 on the east pool — will do a conservative change: rollout to 10% workers first.
deploy-bot: Rolling feature flag change: batching-v2 -> disabled on pool us-east-1 (10% rollout) by Liu at 2026-03-17T09:20:04Z.
Omar (eng-runtime): Also patching the batch-window heuristic to use max-latency budget. Will push a quick canary to staging.
Aaron (oncall-sre): After 10% rollback, p99 for /v1/generate dropped to ~3.5s in the next 5m and admit queue depth started decreasing.
Priya (Acme): We're seeing immediate improvement — thanks. Still some tail, but much better.
Maya (support): Ticket update: inform customer we'll keep them posted, moving to mitigation/resolution.
Omar (eng-runtime): Follow-ups: 1) full rollback of batching-v2 to 0% in us-east if 10% rollback not enough; 2) roll out batch-window fix; 3) add auto-adjust of admission concurrency based on queue growth; 4) add prompt-size override to avoid grouping tiny single-shot prompts into large batches.
Liu (eng-platform): I'll open a change: disable batching-v2 fully on us-east if metrics don't normalize in 15m. Also creating an incident runbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/ingress-batching-backpressure
Maya (support): Priya — we'll schedule a follow-up postmortem and share the runbook and timeline. Anything else from your side?
Priya (Acme): Appreciate the quick turnaround. Please cc our CSM when you have the postmortem.
Aaron (oncall-sre): Monitoring actions: add temporary synthetic load test every 5m on /v1/generate to detect regressions from batching experiments.
Omar (eng-runtime): Patch PR created: reduce batch window default to 5ms and limit max batch size for tiny prompts. PR: https://git.internal/repo/pull/4821
Internal QA Bot: Canary tests passed for PR in staging.
Maya (support): Closing initial escalation — will reopen if customer sees more spikes. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
Priya (Acme): Thanks team :heart:
